title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UC Berkeley (master's, 2027-2028 admissions cycle)
organization: University of California, Berkeley (Center for African Studies), with the Mastercard Foundation
overview: Comprehensive scholarships for citizens of African countries admitted to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less, including Public Policy (MPP), Development Practice (MDP), Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (MS), public health (MPH) and the MBA (with Haas funding). Candidates apply to Berkeley through regular graduate admissions; the programmes nominate candidates to the Scholars Program.
program_dates: Master's programmes of two years or less, admitted in the 2027-2028 admissions cycle (Summer and Fall 2027 admissions)
deadline_text: Scholars Program page: 'September through early January: ... must first apply to the University of California, Berkeley through the regular admissions process. Admission application deadlines vary from September to early January with most in December.' Only first-round applicants (before January) are considered. 'November 15': applicants from African countries who have completed the basic demographic information and named at least two recommenders in the graduate application are invited to apply for application-fee waivers (decisions before 1 December); the page prints no year. February: supplemental application for nominated candidates; March: online interviews; late March or early April: final decisions. The Graduate Division says 'The application for the 2027-2028 admissions cycle is open.'
funding_details: FAQ: 'Mastercard Foundation Scholars receive a comprehensive scholarship equivalent to the costs associated with earning a master's degree, which includes travel, tuition, Berkeley student fees, visa and SEVIS fees, housing, food, living expenses, and cohort signature programs'
Scholars in programmes longer than two semesters do an internship in Africa; the Program pays the round-trip airfare and a living stipend
MBA candidates must also secure Haas scholarships, which requires the Round One deadline
The Scholars Program and some programmes offer a limited number of application-fee waivers
participation_fee: UC Berkeley graduate application fee (amount not read); a limited number of fee waivers for African applicants who complete their basic details and name two recommenders by 15 November
stipend: Living expenses are included (amount not stated)
eligibility: Citizen of an African country, including forcibly displaced people and refugees within Africa; dual citizens and holders of asylee, refugee or permanent-resident status in the US, Canada, UK or EU are not eligible
Admitted to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less (bachelor's and doctoral programmes, and concurrent or dual degrees, do not qualify)
Academic talent, leadership potential and a demonstrated commitment to giving back to your community, country or continent
Has faced significant barriers to accessing higher education (social, financial, personal, practical or health-related)
Intends to return home after the studies and any post-graduation training
Priority, other things being equal: undergraduate degree from an African university, no postgraduate degree yet, not a previous Mastercard Foundation Scholar
Programmes with several admission rounds: only first-round applicants (before January) are considered
nationality_requirements: Citizens of African countries; no country list, so the DRC is included by the general wording
education_requirement: A bachelor's degree and admission to an eligible master's programme
experience_requirement: Set by each master's programme (not read in this cycle)
language_requirement: UC Berkeley graduate admission requirements (not read in this cycle)
other_requirements: Only one programme may be applied to in the 2027-2028 admissions cycle (Graduate Division)
F-1 student visa (from fall 2026, according to the FAQ)
documents_required: UC Berkeley graduate application for the chosen programme (requirements set by the programme)
Scholars Program supplemental application if nominated (February)
application_process: Choose an eligible master's (for example Public Policy MPP, Development Practice MDP, Industrial Engineering and Operations Research MS, an MPH, or the MBA with Haas funding) and check its deadline on the Graduate Division site
Start the 2027-2028 graduate application on gradapp.berkeley.edu; complete the basic demographic information and name at least two recommenders by 15 November to be invited to apply for a fee waiver
Submit by the programme's first-round deadline (most in December, all before January)
February: nominated candidates complete the supplemental application; March: online interviews; late March or early April: final decisions

eligibility_reason: DRC citizenship and a bachelor's degree meet the basic conditions. The award depends on admission to a highly selective Berkeley master's and on barriers to higher education, leadership and a commitment to giving back; the profile does not record the grade, the awarding university or a test score that Berkeley's own admission may require.
potential_issues: Admission to UC Berkeley comes first and is highly competitive; only one programme may be applied to in the cycle
Programme deadlines (most in December) are on the Graduate Division site, not on the Scholars Program page
The fee-waiver step is dated 'November 15' with no year; read with the open 2027-2028 cycle it falls on 15 November 2026
MBA candidates must also win Haas scholarships
Health insurance is not itemised in the FAQ
benefits: Tuition, Berkeley fees, travel, visa and SEVIS fees, housing, food and living expenses
Funded internship in Africa for programmes longer than two semesters
Mastercard Foundation and UC Berkeley alumni networks
relevance_reason: A comprehensive scholarship for Africans at a leading university, with programmes that match the profile (public policy, development practice, operations research, business). Accessibility is low because Berkeley admission is very selective and first-round deadlines fall in December.

visa.support: Visa and SEVIS fees are covered

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: the Berkeley application fee unless a waiver is granted, and any test fees the chosen programme requires
action: If a Berkeley master's such as Public Policy, Development Practice or Operations Research fits, start the 2027-2028 graduate application now: enter your basic details and two recommenders before 15 November to be invited to apply for a fee waiver, then submit by the programme's first-round deadline (mostly December).
notes: Found on 9 November 2026 through a web search (an aggregator gave 15 November 2026 as 'the deadline'; the official page shows that date is the fee-waiver step). Read: the Scholars Program graduate process, eligibility and FAQ pages and the Graduate Division apply page.
